subject: [PATCH v2 0/3] mm: make watermark checks honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT

reviews.author: Harry Yoo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Harry Yoo pointed out that the changelog should be more concise, specifically highlighting the key issue that __zone_watermark_ok() needs to consider the allocation's migrate type when defrag_mode is enabled, and suggested additional explanations for why direct compaction and reclamation are affected prematurely.

Reviewer Harry Yoo noted that the patch otherwise looks good, but requested a minor improvement and provided a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
nit: perhaps we could make the changelog above bit more concise.

I think the necessary bit here is "With defrag_mode, allocations cannot
steal a page from pageblocks of other migrate type, thus
__zone_watermark_ok() needs to take that into account."

... and maybe

- "Ignoring the allocation's migrate type leads to
   stopping direct compaction and reclamation prematurely".

- "Indirect compaction and reclamation are not affected as they do not
   serve specific allocations"

---

otherwise looks good to me,
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Meta) <harry@kernel.org>

with a nit below.

2026-11-05.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a performance issue in Linux kernel's memory management, specifically when using defrag_mode and 64K mTHP (machine-specific transparent huge pages). The high-order watermark check was not honoring the ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT flag, leading to stalls in compaction and inefficient direct reclaim. The patches modify the watermark check to consider the request's migratetype and skip free lists that cannot be used by the request. Additionally, patch 3 informs direct reclaim about the allocation type. This change improves performance by reducing compaction stalls and increasing the efficiency of direct reclaim.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
Author corrected the terminology used in the patch description to accurately reflect that ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT is a property of normal zone allocations, not defrag_mode, and provided an alternative version of the code.

The author is addressing a concern that kcompactd_node_suitable() does not pass the migratetype to __zone_watermark_ok_mt(). The author explains that this function only uses the migratetype under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT and that no functional change will occur with the addition of __zone_watermark_ok_mt(), which takes the migratetype. A new changelog is provided, indicating preparation for making the high-order check honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT.
reviews.raw_body:
It is ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, not defrag_mode: Normal zone allocations get it
on the first attempt when DMA32 is populated, with defrag_mode off. And
such an allocation can still claim a whole free pageblock of another
migratetype.

But fair, it can be shorter. A tighter version is below; it also says
why kcompactd passes MIGRATE_MOVABLE.

---

The value is not read there: __zone_watermark_ok_mt() uses the
migratetype only under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, and kcompactd never passes it.
kcompactd_node_suitable() makes the same call and has no compact_control
to take it from.

Thanks for the review.

The new changelog:

	The high-order check in __zone_watermark_ok() accepts a free page of any
	migratetype.  Under ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT, a request below pageblock_order can
	only take a page of its own migratetype or claim a whole free block, so
	the check can pass when the allocation cannot succeed.

	Only a check whether one allocation can be served now should count just
	the pages it can take.  A check whether a zone has enough free memory
	serves no single allocation and counts every migratetype: reclaim and
	compaction free whole pageblocks across migratetypes.

	Add __zone_watermark_ok_mt(), which takes the migratetype, for the first
	kind:

	  - the allocator fast path, zone_watermark_fast();
	  - its recheck after node reclaim in get_page_from_freelist();
	  - compaction's up-front check, compaction_suit_allocation_order().

	__zone_watermark_ok() wraps it for the second kind.  kcompactd shares
	compaction_suit_allocation_order() with direct compaction and passes
	MIGRATE_MOVABLE, which is not read without ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT.

	Declare both in mm/internal.h: nothing outside mm uses them.

	Nothing reads the migratetype yet: no functional change.  Preparation for
	making the high-order check honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT.

Looks good?

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Vlastimil suggested passing the entire alloc_flags value to try_to_free_pages() instead of modifying it, and otherwise approved the patch (LGTM)
reviews.raw_body:
I'd perhaps pass whole alloc_flags to try_to_free_pages(), but other than
that LGTM.
